summary: Proves a height inequality h_S(π(P)) ≤ c(1 + ĥ_𝒜(P)) on X* for every subvariety X of an abelian scheme over a curve over Q̄, where X* removes the generically special subvarieties (Theorem 1.4). As an application it proves the Geometric Bogomolov Conjecture over function fields of curves in characteristic 0 (Theorem 1.1). The proof shows that degenerate subvarieties, those where the Betti map has positive-dimensional fibres, are generically special (Theorem 5.1), using monodromy, Deligne's semisimplicity and Pila–Wilkie. Then an auxiliary variety, Blichfeldt lattice counting on Betti coordinates and Habegger's degree-height lemma give h([2^N]P) ≥ c4^N h(P) − c′(N) (Proposition 9.1), and Silverman–Tate kills the error term. Silverman's limit theorem gives Theorem 1.1, and Moriwaki heights extend it to all characteristic-0 constant fields. The atlas plans heights, Manin–Mumford, Blichfeldt, Néron models and o-minimality; it lacks function-field heights, the trace, Betti maps, variations of Hodge structure, Moriwaki heights and the height inequality.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (Geometric Bogomolov Conjecture over Q̄(S))
items.statement: Let K be the function field of a smooth projective curve over k = Q̄, A an abelian variety over K with symmetric ample L, and X ⊆ A an irreducible closed subvariety with X ⊗_K K̄ irreducible and not of the form B + (Z ⊗_k K̄) with Z ⊆ A^{K̄/k} closed irreducible and B a torsion coset of A ⊗_K K̄. Then there is ε > 0 such that {x ∈ X(K̄) : ĥ_{K,A,L}(x) ≤ ε} is not Zariski dense in X.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p.2; proof §11, pp.52–54, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Proof: spread out to 𝒜 → S with an admissible immersion, apply Proposition 10.1 to the Zariski closure of X, and compare with Silverman's Height Limit Theorem 11.1 along the section of each small point; the bound is ĥ_{K,A}(x) ≥ deg(S)/c off a proper closed subset.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 for every algebraically closed k of characteristic 0 (Appendix A)
items.statement: Theorem 1.1 holds with Q̄ replaced by any algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0.
items.locator: Appendix A, §A.3, pp.56–57, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (a sketch)
items.note: Descend to a finitely generated k₀, run §11 with Moriwaki heights (Theorem A.3 and the Moriwaki–Wazir Silverman theorems), and pass from k₀‾(S) to K through the essential minimum: µ_ess(X) = 0 iff ĥ(X) = 0 (Zhang, Gubler Cor. 4.4) and ĥ(X) is invariant under extension of the constant field. The authors call this a sketch.

items.name: The K/k-trace and trace map (Chow)
items.statement: For a field extension K/k with k algebraically closed in K and char k = 0, and an abelian variety A over K, the K/k-trace A^{K/k} is an abelian variety over k with a trace map τ : A^{K/k} ⊗_k K → A universal for maps from constant abelian varieties; τ is a closed immersion in characteristic 0, and there is a unique abelian subvariety A′ ⊆ A with A′ = A^{K/k} ⊗ K and (A/A′)^{K/k} = 0.
items.locator: §1, p.2; §2, p.9; §3.1, p.12, citing Conrad [Con06, §6, Thms. 6.2, 6.4], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Not in the atlas. Routed with Lang–Néron to HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.1 as a source.

items.name: Lang–Néron theorem
items.statement: If L/k is a finitely generated extension with k algebraically closed in L and A is an abelian variety over L with A^{L/k} = 0, then A(L) is a finitely generated abelian group.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.1, p.14, and of Proposition B.1, p.58, citing Lang–Néron [LN59, Thm. 1] and [Con06, Thm. 7.1], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: The function-field Mordell–Weil theorem. Routed to RP.1 as a source.

items.name: Heights over the function field of a curve
items.statement: For K = k(S̄), S̄ a smooth projective irreducible curve over an algebraically closed k, the height h_K : ℙ^n(K̄) → ℝ, h_K(P) = [K′:K]^{-1} Σ_v d_v log max_i |p_i|_v for P = [p₀:…:p_n] with p_i ∈ K′ finite over K, summing over the places of K′ above S̄(k); it satisfies the product formula and is independent of K′.
items.locator: §2.1, pp.9–10, citing Bombieri–Gubler §1.3, 1.4.6 and [Con06, §8], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: The atlas height owner (RP.0) plans number-field heights; the function-field height is routed there as a source.

items.name: Néron–Tate height over a function field and its kernel
items.statement: For A over K = k(S̄) with symmetric ample L, Tate's limit gives ĥ_{K,A,L} : A(K̄) → [0,∞), a quadratic form, and ĥ_{K,A,L}(P) = 0 iff P ∈ (A^{K̄/k} ⊗_k K̄)(K̄) + A_tor.
items.note: The kernel statement combines Lang–Néron with Northcott for constant heights. Routed to RP.0 as a source.

items.name: Definition 1.2 (generically special subvariety) and X*
items.statement: For an abelian scheme 𝒜 → S over a smooth irreducible curve over k, an irreducible closed Y ⊆ 𝒜 is generically special if it dominates S and its geometric generic fibre is a finite union of (Z ⊗_k k(S)‾) + B with Z ⊆ A^{k(S)‾/k} closed irreducible and B a torsion coset. For irreducible closed X ⊆ 𝒜, X* = X minus the union of the generically special Y ⊆ X.
items.locator: Definition 1.2 and the display below it, p.3, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 1.3 (maximal generically special subvarieties)
items.statement: Only finitely many generically special subvarieties of 𝒜 contained in X are maximal for this property. Hence X* is Zariski open in X, and X* = ∅ iff X is generically special.
items.locator: Proposition 1.3, p.3; proof §3.1, p.12, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Via the Poincaré splitting A′ × A″ → A with A′ the trace part and (A″)^{K/k} = 0, and Proposition 3.1 with V₀ = A^{K/k}. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Absolute logarithmic Weil height on ℙ^n(Q̄)
items.statement: h([p₀:…:p_n]) = [K:ℚ]^{-1} Σ_v d_v log max_i |p_i|_v for p_i in a number field K, independent of K and of the coordinates.
items.locator: §2.1, p.9, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Mathlib `Projectivization.logHeight` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/Projectivization.lean:51) for fields with `Height.AdmissibleAbsValues`; the extension to Q̄ is RP.0 work.

items.name: Height machine on quasi-projective varieties
items.statement: To (S̄, M) with M ample the Height Machine attaches h_{S̄,M} : S(Q̄) → ℝ, well defined up to O(1), which may be taken ≥ 0, with additivity, functoriality and h(ϕ(Q)) ≤ δh(Q) + c(ϕ) for a rational map ϕ given by forms of degree δ, off their common zeros.
items.locator: §1, p.3; §2.2, p.11; (9.2), p.50, citing Bombieri–Gubler Ch. 2.4 and Hindry–Silverman Thm. B.2.5(a), arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: RP.0 plans divisor/line-bundle heights modulo bounded functions and their pullback and tensor laws.

items.name: Naive and fibrewise Néron–Tate heights on an abelian scheme
items.statement: For P = (P′, π(P)) ∈ 𝒜(Q̄) ⊆ ℙ^M × ℙ^m, h(P) = h(P′) + h(π(P)) (2.2); the fibrewise Néron–Tate height ĥ_𝒜(P) = ĥ_{𝒜_{π(P)}}(P) = lim h([2^N]P)/4^N (2.1), (2.3), quadratic on each fibre.
items.note: RP.0 plans the height machine and Néron–Tate heights.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 (height inequality over a curve)
items.statement: Let π : 𝒜 → S be an abelian scheme over a smooth irreducible curve over Q̄, L a relatively ample symmetric line bundle and M ample on a compactification S̄. For every closed irreducible X ⊆ 𝒜 over Q̄ there is c > 0 with h_{S̄,M}(π(P)) ≤ c(1 + ĥ_{𝒜,L}(P)) for all P ∈ X*(Q̄).
items.locator: Theorem 1.4 and (1.1), p.4; proof §10.2, p.52, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Induction on dim X: Proposition 10.1 on an open dense U ⊆ X and the induction hypothesis on the components Z_i of X∖U, using X* ⊆ (X∖Z) ∪ ⋃ Z_i* (10.4). Generalized to bases of any dimension by Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger 2021, Theorems 1.6/B.1.

items.name: Theorem 1.4′ (with the naive height)
items.statement: With L′ = L ⊗ π*M and a closed immersion ι : 𝒜 → ℙ^M × S from (L′)^{⊗n}, h_{𝒜,L′}(P) = n^{-1}h(P′) + h_{S̄,M}(π(P)); then h_{S̄,M}(π(P)) ≤ h_{𝒜,L′}(P) ≤ c(1 + ĥ_{𝒜,L}(P)) for all P ∈ X*(Q̄).
items.locator: Theorem 1.4′, p.5; proof §10.2, p.52, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (the first inequality is misattributed to (1.1), sourceIssues E15)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Projective presentation of an abelian scheme over a curve
items.statement: For an abelian scheme 𝒜 → S over a smooth curve and a symmetric ample L on the generic fibre, L^{⊗3g} gives a projectively normal closed immersion of the generic fibre; after removing finitely many points of S its Zariski closure in ℙ^M_S is an abelian scheme isomorphic to 𝒜, giving ι_S : 𝒜 → ℙ^M × S with relatively very ample ι_S*O(1). In general a closed immersion 𝒜 → ℙ^M × S arises from (L ⊗ π*M)^{⊗n}, n ≫ 1 (Raynaud, Faisceaux amples XI 1.4; EGA II 5.3.3, 4.1.4).
items.note: Routed to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 as a source.

items.name: Néron mapping property for abelian schemes
items.statement: An abelian scheme over a Dedekind (here smooth curve) base is the Néron model of its generic fibre, so morphisms from the generic fibre extend. For an abelian subvariety A₀ of the generic fibre, the Néron model of A/A₀ is an abelian scheme ℬ with an exact sequence 0 → A₀-model → 𝒜 → ℬ → 0 (BLR §1.2 Prop. 8, §7.5 Prop. 3).
items.locator: §2.2, p.10; proof of Theorem 5.1, p.29, citing [BLR90], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1 plans Néron models over Dedekind bases, the mapping property, extension of homomorphisms and the comparison with abelian-scheme models.

items.name: Multiplication by 2 by quartic polynomials in families
items.statement: On the projectively normal generic fibre with [2]*L ≅ L^{⊗4}, [2] is given by M+1 forms of degree 4; after removing finitely many points of S, [2] on 𝒜 ⊆ ℙ^M × ℙ^m is given by bihomogeneous G₀,…,G_M of degree 4 in X and c₀ in Y (A2), and [2^N] locally by forms of degree 4^N in X and ≤ c₁(4^N − 1)/3 in the base coordinates.
items.locator: §2.2 (A2), p.11; §9.1, p.47; proof of Proposition 9.1, p.49, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source, as for PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21.

items.name: Admissible immersion (A1)–(A3)
items.statement: An immersion 𝒜 → ℙ^M × ℙ^m compatible with π and the projection, such that (A1) each 𝒜_s → ℙ^M is induced by a symmetric very ample bundle, (A2) [2] is given by bihomogeneous polynomials of degree 4 in the fibre coordinates, and (A3) for every s and P ∈ 𝒜_s a generic hyperplane section of 𝒜_s through P contains no positive-dimensional coset. Every abelian variety over k(S) is, after shrinking S, the generic fibre of an abelian scheme with an admissible immersion.
items.note: (A3) comes from Proposition C.1 with d = g for the L^{⊗3} embedding. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (special points of V₀(k) × A_tor)
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic 0, S a smooth irreducible curve over k, K = k(S)‾, A an abelian variety over K with A^{K/k} = 0, V₀ an irreducible variety over k, V = V₀ ⊗_k K and Σ = V₀(k) × A_tor. (i) If Y ⊆ V × A is irreducible closed with Y(K) ∩ Σ Zariski dense, then Y = (W₀ ⊗_k K) × (P + B) with W₀ ⊆ V₀ irreducible closed, P ∈ A_tor and B an abelian subvariety. (ii) Only finitely many such subvarieties contained in a given Y are maximal.
items.locator: Proposition 3.1 and proof, pp.12–15, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprints E1–E3)
items.note: Uniform Manin–Mumford (Theorem 3.2) gives finitely many B; a Galois-orbit bound and Proposition B.1 bound the orders; then [N] ∘ (A → A/B) and the fibre dimension theorem. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Theorem 3.2 (uniform Manin–Mumford in characteristic 0)
items.statement: For an abelian variety A and an irreducible quasi-projective V over K, and Y ⊆ V × A irreducible closed with fibres Y_v = projection of Y ∩ ({v} × A), there are a finite set 𝓜 of abelian subvarieties and D such that for every v ∈ V(K̄) the Zariski closure of Y_v(K̄) ∩ A_tor is a union of at most D translates of members of 𝓜 by torsion points.
items.locator: Theorem 3.2 and proof, p.13, citing Raynaud [Ray83], Scanlon [Sca04, Thm. 2.4], Hrushovski [Hru01], Hindry [Hin88, Thm. 1], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (statement misprint E1)
items.note: Routed to HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.5 as a source; RP.5 plans the qualitative Manin–Mumford theorem, and uniformity in algebraic families is Scanlon's automatic uniformity.

items.name: Manin–Mumford conjecture in characteristic 0 (Raynaud)
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 and a subvariety X ⊆ A, the Zariski closure of X ∩ A_tor is a finite union of torsion cosets.
items.locator: §1, p.3; proof of Theorem 3.2, p.13, citing [Ray83], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: RP.5 plans the Manin–Mumford theorem with precise characteristic and field hypotheses.

items.name: Torsion points are unramified at places of good reduction (residue characteristic 0)
items.statement: If an abelian variety over the function field F of a curve over k (char 0) has good reduction at a place v, then F(P)/F is unramified at v for every torsion point P.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.1, p.14 ("general reduction theory of abelian varieties"), arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5 plans Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich; the needed direction is its easy half.

items.name: Lemma B.2 (finitely many étale covers of bounded degree)
items.statement: For a smooth irreducible quasi-projective variety S over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0, the étale fundamental group π₁(S) is topologically finitely generated; hence S has only finitely many étale coverings of degree ≤ D, and the compositum of all extensions of k(S) of degree ≤ D unramified over S is finite. A finite monodromy representation is trivialized on a finite étale cover (Riemann existence).
items.locator: Lemma B.2 and proof, p.58, citing SGA1 XII 5.1, XIII 2.12, Cadoret [Cad13, Cor. 6.5, Rem. 6.8], Völklein [Völ96, Cor. 7.11]; proof of Proposition 3.1, p.14; proof of Lemma 5.8, p.26, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Descend to a subfield of finite transcendence degree, compare with ℂ, use finite generation of π₁^top and Riemann existence, and invariance of π₁ under extension of algebraically closed fields. Routed to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0 as a source.

items.name: Proposition B.1 (torsion of bounded degree has bounded order)
items.statement: If S is smooth irreducible quasi-projective over k (char 0, algebraically closed), K = k(S) and A/K has A^{K/k} = 0, then the orders of the points of {P ∈ A(K̄)_tor : [K(P):K] ≤ D} are bounded in terms of A and D.
items.locator: Proposition B.1 and proof, p.58; the case dim S = 1 is the claim (3.2), p.14, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: The Zariski closure of a torsion point is a component of 𝒜[N], hence finite étale over S; Lemma B.2 bounds the compositum and Lang–Néron finishes. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition B.3 (Proposition 3.1 over a base of any dimension)
items.statement: Proposition 3.1(i) holds with S smooth irreducible quasi-projective of any dimension over k.
items.locator: Proposition B.3, p.59, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: The only use of dim S = 1 in Proposition 3.1 is (3.2), replaced by Proposition B.1. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 4.1 and Remark 4.2 (the Betti map over a curve)
items.statement: For an abelian scheme π : 𝒜 → S of relative dimension g over a smooth irreducible complex curve and s ∈ S(ℂ), there are an open neighbourhood Δ of s in S^an and a real-analytic b : 𝒜_Δ → T^{2g} with (i) b|_{𝒜_s^an} a group isomorphism for all s ∈ Δ, (ii) every fibre b^{-1}(ξ) complex analytic, (iii) (b, π) : 𝒜_Δ → T^{2g} × Δ real bianalytic. For path-connected Δ two such maps differ by an element of GL_{2g}(ℤ).
items.locator: Proposition 4.1, Remark 4.2 and construction, pp.15–18, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Construction: Ehresmann trivialization with analytic fibres, a holomorphic period matrix from Griffiths' theorem, and the Albanese coordinates b̃(P) = (Ω, Ω̄)^{-1}(L(P), L̄(P)) ∈ ℝ^{2g}. The special case of PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 Proposition 2.1/B.2. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Ehresmann trivialization with analytic fibres and holomorphic periods
items.statement: For a proper submersion 𝒜^an → S^an there is, locally on S, a fibrewise diffeomorphism 𝒜_{s₀} × Δ ≅ 𝒜_Δ whose inverse has complex-analytic fibres (Voisin I, Thm. 9.3, Prop. 9.5); the Hodge subspace f_s* H⁰(𝒜_s, Ω¹) ⊆ H¹(𝒜_{s₀}, ℂ) varies holomorphically in s (Griffiths), so the period matrix Ω(s) is holomorphic.
items.locator: §4, pp.15–17, citing Voisin [Voi02, Thm. 9.3, Prop. 9.5] and Griffiths, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to the Hodge-theory Part II DegeneratingHodgeStructures (period maps of variations).

items.name: Degenerate points and degenerate subvarieties (base a curve)
items.statement: For Y ⊆ 𝒜 irreducible closed dominating S and a Betti map b on 𝒜_Δ, P ∈ Y^{sm,an} ∩ 𝒜_Δ is degenerate for Y if it is not isolated in b|_{Y^{sm,an} ∩ 𝒜_Δ}^{-1}(b(P)); Y is degenerate if a non-empty open subset of Y^{sm,an} ∩ 𝒜_Δ consists of degenerate points.
items.locator: §5, p.18, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: For dim S = 1 this is the negation of the Betti-rank condition of PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 Definition 1.5. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (degenerate implies generically special)
items.statement: Over a smooth irreducible complex curve S, an irreducible closed subvariety of 𝒜 that is degenerate is generically special.
items.locator: Theorem 5.1, p.18; proof §5.4, pp.28–30, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprint E9; Lemma 5.8 gap E8)
items.note: Pass to a finite étale cover where the trace is stable and Lemma 5.7 applies; monodromy transport (Proposition 5.4) makes Y virtually monodromy invariant over uncountably many extendable points; Lemma 5.8 when the trace vanishes; the general case splits off the constant part via the Néron model of A/A₀ and uses Proposition 1.3. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: The o-minimal structure ℝ_an and definable sets
items.statement: ℝ_an, generated by restrictions to [−1,1]^n of real-analytic functions, is o-minimal; definable sets and families in it.
items.locator: §5.1, pp.18–19, citing van den Dries [vdD98], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6 plans the selected o-minimal structures, definable sets and cell decomposition.

items.name: Semi-rational Pila–Wilkie counting in definable families (Habegger–Pila)
items.statement: For a definable family Z ⊆ ℝ^m × ℝ^n with fibres Z_x and ε > 0 there is c such that if a fibre contains more than cT^ε points whose "rational" coordinates have height ≤ T, then there is a continuous definable path whose rational coordinates are semi-algebraic and whose remaining coordinates are non-constant, starting at such a point ([HP16, Cor. 7.2], including the refinement (iii) that the path starts at a rational point).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.2, pp.19–20, citing Habegger–Pila [HP16, Cor. 7.2], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: LD.6 plans the plain Pila–Wilkie estimate; the semi-rational family version is routed to LD.6 as a source.

items.name: Ax's theorem for complex abelian varieties (Ax-type images)
items.statement: For a complex abelian variety A with real-analytic group isomorphism A^an → T^{2g}, the image of X(ℂ) for Zariski closed X is definable and of Ax-type: every continuous semi-algebraic path y : [0,1] → exp^{-1}(image), real-analytic on (0,1), satisfies exp ∘ y([0,1]) ⊆ y(0) + G ⊆ image for a closed subgroup G.
items.locator: §5.1, p.19; proof of Proposition 5.3, p.21, citing Ax [Ax71], [Ax72], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Functional transcendence for a constant abelian variety. Routed to LD.6 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.2 (invariant definable sets of Ax-type)
items.statement: Let X ⊆ T^n be closed, definable and of Ax-type, and Γ ⊆ GL_n(ℤ) free on two generators with γ(X) = X for all γ ∈ Γ. Then either X lies in a finite union of proper closed subgroups of T^n, or there are a non-empty open U ⊆ X and a closed connected infinite subgroup G with U + G ⊆ X.
items.locator: Lemma 5.2 and proof, pp.19–20, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprints E4–E5)
items.note: Exponential growth of Γ (≥ T^{log 2/log c₁} elements of height ≤ T) against semi-rational Pila–Wilkie, then Ax-type, Kronecker's countability of closed subgroups and Baire. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Proposition 5.3 (monodromy-invariant subvarieties of an abelian variety)
items.statement: Let A be a complex abelian variety and Γ ⊆ GL_{2g}(ℤ) act continuously on A^an via a Betti isomorphism, of monodromy type (every abelian subvariety is Γ-stable), containing a free subgroup of rank 2 and with no non-zero invariant vector in ℤ^{2g}. If Z ⊆ A is irreducible closed with Γ(Z(ℂ)) = Z(ℂ), then Z lies in a proper torsion coset, or Z + B = Z for some abelian subvariety B of positive dimension.
items.locator: Proposition 5.3 and proof, pp.21–22, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Poincaré complementary abelian subvariety
items.statement: For an abelian subvariety B of a polarized abelian variety A there is a complementary B′ with B + B′ = A and B ∩ B′ finite.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.3, p.21; §3.1, p.12; proof of Theorem 5.1, p.29, citing Birkenhake–Lange [BL04, §5.3], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6 plans Poincaré complete reducibility.

items.name: Proposition 5.4 (monodromy transport along Betti fibres)
items.statement: Glueing Betti maps along loops gives a homomorphism ρ̃ : π₁(S^an, s) → {homeomorphic group automorphisms of 𝒜_s^an} with ρ̃(h)_* = ρ(h), the monodromy on H₁(𝒜_s^an, ℤ). (i) If P ∈ Y^an over s is not isolated in its Betti fibre in Y, then ρ̃(h)(P) ∈ Y^an for all h, and if P has order N then dim_P Y ∩ 𝒜[N] ≥ 1. (ii) ρ̃ commutes with homomorphisms of abelian schemes.
items.locator: Proposition 5.4, (5.3)–(5.5) and proof, pp.22–24, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprint E6)
items.note: Uses dim S = 1: the Betti fibre through a degenerate point is a disc contained in Y by the identity lemma. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Deligne: semisimplicity of monodromy and the Theorem of the Fixed Part
items.statement: For a family of abelian varieties over a smooth complex curve, the identity component G⁰_s of the Zariski closure of the monodromy group in GL(H₁(𝒜_s, ℚ)) is semisimple (Hodge II, Cor. 4.2.9), and the monodromy invariants H₁(𝒜_s, ℤ)^ρ carry a sub-Hodge structure (Cor. 4.1.2); the isomorphism class of G_s and the index [G_s : G⁰_s] do not depend on s.
items.locator: §5.3, pp.25–26, citing Deligne [Del71, 4.1.2, 4.2.9] and Zarhin [Zar08], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to the Hodge-theory Part II DegeneratingHodgeStructures.

items.name: Tits: free subgroups of linear groups
items.statement: A subgroup of GL_n over a field of characteristic 0 that is not virtually solvable contains a free subgroup on two generators; in particular a Zariski-dense subgroup of a non-trivial connected semisimple group does ([Tit72, Thm. 3]).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.5, p.25, citing Tits [Tit72, Thm. 3], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: No atlas layer owns the Tits alternative; it is routed with its only consumer, Lemma 5.5, to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Lemma 5.5 (free subgroups in monodromy)
items.statement: If G⁰_s is non-trivial, every finite-index subgroup of Γ_s = ρ(π₁(S^an, s)) contains a free subgroup on two generators.
items.locator: Lemma 5.5 and proof, p.25, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Tits applied to Γ′ ∩ G⁰_s(ℚ), Zariski dense in G⁰_s. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Hodge substructures of H₁ come from abelian subvarieties
items.statement: Rational (or integral) Hodge substructures of H₁(A^an, ℤ) for a complex abelian variety A correspond to abelian subvarieties B ⊆ A, with dim B = ½ rank.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.6, p.25, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A5 plans the equivalence between polarized complex abelian varieties and polarizable integral Hodge structures of types (−1,0),(0,−1).

items.name: Grothendieck: extension of homomorphisms of abelian schemes
items.statement: For abelian schemes ℬ, 𝒜 over a smooth connected complex base S and s ∈ S(ℂ), every homomorphism ℬ_s → 𝒜_s whose map on H₁ is monodromy-equivariant is the restriction of a homomorphism ℬ → 𝒜 over S (Grothendieck, Invent. Math. 2 (1966); Deligne Hodge II 4.1.3.2).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.6, p.25, citing [Gro66] and [Del71, 4.1.3.2], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6 (Hom groups and their compatibility with geometric fibres) as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.6 (invariant homology forces a non-zero trace)
items.statement: If H₁(𝒜_s^an, ℤ) has a non-zero monodromy-invariant element, then the ℂ(S)‾/ℂ-trace of the generic fibre is non-zero.
items.locator: Lemma 5.6 and proof, p.25, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: The invariants give an abelian subvariety B ⊆ 𝒜_s by the Theorem of the Fixed Part; Grothendieck's theorem extends B × S → 𝒜. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Extendable points and Lemma 5.7 (Zarhin)
items.statement: s ∈ S(ℂ) is extendable for 𝒜 if every abelian subvariety of 𝒜_s is the fibre of an abelian subscheme (the image of an endomorphism of 𝒜). If G⁰_s = G_s for some s, then all points outside an at most countable subset of S(ℂ) are extendable; they are the Hodge-generic points.
items.locator: §5.3 and Lemma 5.7, pp.25–26, citing Zarhin [Zar08, Cor. 3.5], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Hodge loci of the variation. Routed to the Hodge-theory Part II DegeneratingHodgeStructures.

items.name: Lemma 5.8 (virtually monodromy-invariant subvarieties lie in kernels)
items.statement: Let Y ⊆ 𝒜 be irreducible closed dominating S, virtually monodromy invariant (some component of Y_s is ρ̃-stable under a finite-index subgroup) above every point of an uncountable set of extendable points, and suppose the generic fibre of 𝒜 ×_S S′ has trivial trace for every finite étale S′ → S. Then there is a homomorphism 𝒜 → 𝒞 of abelian schemes over S whose kernel contains Y and has dimension dim Y.
items.locator: Lemma 5.8 and proof, pp.26–28, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprint E7; degenerate cases of the induction omitted, E8)
items.note: Induction on dim 𝒜 with Proposition 5.3 at uncountably many points: torsion cosets give [N]Y ⊆ ℬ (Case 1), stabilizers give a quotient 𝒜/ℬ (Case 2). The subcases where ℬ or 𝒜/ℬ has relative dimension 0 need the one-line arguments in sourceIssues E8. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Lemma 6.2 (non-generically special subvarieties have full Betti rank)
items.statement: If X ⊆ 𝒜 dominating S is not generically special, there is P ∈ X^{sm}(F) with π(P) ∈ Δ and P ∈ (X_{π(P)})^{sm} such that dim im T_P(b|_{X^{sm,an} ∩ 𝒜_Δ}) = 2 dim X (6.1).
items.locator: Lemma 6.2 and proof, p.31, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Theorem 5.1 makes X non-degenerate; the constant-rank theorem then forces maximal rank 2 dim X, and F-points are dense. Routed to the Betti-map Part II.

items.name: Proposition 6.1 (the auxiliary subvariety Z)
items.statement: For X ⊊ 𝒜 dominating S, not generically special, of codimension n, and P as in (6.1), there is an irreducible closed Z ⊆ 𝒜 over F with (i) dim Z = n and Z dominating S, (ii) P smooth on Z_s and Z, (iii) Z_s containing no positive-dimensional coset, (iv) deg Z_t ≤ D for all t, and (v) im T_P(b|_X) ∩ im T_P(b|_{Z_s}) = 0. Moreover only finitely many fibres Z_t contain a positive-dimensional coset.
items.locator: Proposition 6.1, pp.30–31; proof §§6.1–6.4, pp.31–38, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Z is a component of (𝒵(f₁,…,f_{g+1−n}) × ℙ^m) ∩ 𝒜 for generic linear forms through P, using (A3), Bertini, Bézout and Lemma 6.6; the Moreover part is Proposition 6.9. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Bertini theorems for generic linear sections through a point
items.statement: For an irreducible closed V ⊆ ℙ^M smooth at P, generic linear forms f₁,…,f_r vanishing at P cut V in a set smooth at P of dimension dim V − r, irreducible if dim V − r ≥ 1; generic here means in a Zariski open dense set of coefficient vectors.
items.locator: §6.1, pp.31–32, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Flatness and fibre dimension over a smooth curve
items.statement: An irreducible closed subvariety dominating a smooth curve is flat over it with equidimensional fibres of dimension one less (Hartshorne III.9.6, 9.7); fibre dimension theorem (Hartshorne Ex. II.3.22).
items.note: Routed to SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 as a source.

items.name: Lemmas 6.3–6.6 (transversal complex subspaces)
items.statement: Let T be a g-dimensional ℂ-vector space and W ⊆ T of dimension m. (6.3) A real subspace V₀ ⊆ T_ℝ of dimension 2m+2k containing W meets some complex subspace of dimension g − (m+k) trivially. (6.4–6.5) Base cases: ℂ^{2k} has a k-dimensional complex subspace meeting ℝ^{2k} trivially. (6.6) If dim_ℝ V = 2(m+1) and W ⊆ V, the complex subspaces V′ of dimension g − m − 1 with V′ ∩ V = 0 form a non-empty open subset of Gr(T, g−m−1).
items.locator: Lemmas 6.3–6.6 and proofs, pp.32–34, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprint E10)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II with Proposition 6.1.

items.name: Lemma 6.8 (Faltings: cutting out by hypersurfaces of bounded degree)
items.statement: An irreducible closed subvariety of ℙ^n of degree δ is an intersection of finitely many irreducible hypersurfaces of degree ≤ δ.
items.locator: Lemma 6.8, p.35, citing Faltings [Fal91, Prop. 2.1], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 6.7 (Bézout for long intersections)
items.statement: If V₁,…,V_m ⊆ ℙ^n are irreducible closed of degree ≤ δ and C₁,…,C_r are the top-dimensional (dimension k) components of V₁ ∩ ⋯ ∩ V_m, then Σ deg C_i ≤ δ^{n−k}, independently of m.
items.locator: Proposition 6.7 and proof, pp.35–36, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Choose n−k hypersurfaces of degree δ in general position through C₁ ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_r and apply Bézout. The proof also works when each V_i is reducible with the sum of its component degrees ≤ δ, which is how it is used in Proposition 6.9 (sourceIssues E12). Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Bézout and conservation of number (Fulton)
items.statement: The degrees of the irreducible components of an intersection in ℙ^n sum to at most the product of the degrees (Fulton Ex. 8.4.6, also for reducible hypersurfaces); degrees of fibres of a flat family of cycles are constant (Fulton 10.2.2).
items.locator: §6.1, p.32; proof of Proposition 6.7, p.36; §8.3, p.46, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to SF.5 as a source.

items.name: Degree of stabilizers (David–Hindry)
items.statement: For an irreducible subvariety W of an abelian variety embedded in projective space, the stabilizer Stab(W) has degree ≤ deg(W)^{dim W + 1} ([DH00, Lemme 2.1(ii)]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.9, p.38; proof of Proposition 8.1, p.47, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to RP.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 6.9 (few fibres contain cosets)
items.statement: If Z ⊆ 𝒜 is irreducible closed dominating S and some fibre Z_s contains no positive-dimensional coset, then only finitely many fibres Z_t contain a positive-dimensional coset.
items.locator: Proposition 6.9 and proof, pp.36–38, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprint E11; Proposition 6.7 applied to reducible fibres, E12)
items.note: For a large prime ℓ and each ℓ-torsion section σ, Z(σ) = ⋂_k (Z − [k]σ) is closed and contains every coset-bearing fibre; Proposition 6.7 bounds the top-dimensional part of Z(σ)_s independently of ℓ, and the stabilizer bound gives a contradiction if Z(σ)_s ≠ ∅. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Blichfeldt's theorem
items.statement: If U ⊆ ℝ^m is measurable, some translate −x + U contains at least vol(U) points of ℤ^m.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.2, p.41, citing Cassels [Cas97, III.2, Thm. I], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.1 plans Blichfeldt and Minkowski.

items.name: Lemma 7.1 (volume and injectivity of ψ_N)
items.statement: For C¹ maps φ₁ : U₀ × U₁ → ℝ^m, φ₂ : U₀ × U₂ → ℝ^m (U₀ ⊆ ℝ², m = 2 + m₁ + m₂) with finite C¹ norms, ψ_N(w,x,y) = Nφ₁(w,x) − φ₂(w,y), and z₀ with δ₀(z₀) ≠ 0 (7.2), there are bounded neighbourhoods U″ ⊆ U′ of z₀ and c ∈ (0,1] such that φ₁ is injective on π₁(U′) and, for N ≥ c^{-1}, ψ_N|_{U′} is injective and open, vol ψ_N(U″) ≥ cN^{2+m₁} and B_c(ψ_N(U″)) ⊆ ψ_N(U′).
items.locator: Lemma 7.1 and proof, pp.38–41, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprints E13)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 7.2 (lattice points in ψ_N(U′))
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 7.1 there are a bounded neighbourhood U′ of z₀ and c ∈ (0,1] with #(ψ_N(U′) ∩ N₀^{-1}ℤ^m) ≥ cN^{2+m₁} for all integers N₀ ≥ c^{-1} and real N ≥ c^{-1}; moreover φ₁|_{π₁(U′)} and ψ_N|_{U′} are injective.
items.locator: Proposition 7.2 and proof, p.41, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Blichfeldt, then translation by a point of N₀^{-1}ℤ^m within c of the Blichfeldt shift. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Lemma 8.2 (division points from lattice points)
items.statement: For X as in Proposition 8.1 there are c > 0, a prime ℓ > D^{2^{g+1}(g+1)} and a finite étale S′ → S carrying all ℓ-torsion sections such that for every N ≥ c^{-1} there are r ≥ cN^{2 dim X} pairs (P′_i, Q′_i) ∈ X′(ℂ) × Z′(ℂ), with the P′_i distinct, satisfying (i) π′(P′_i) = π′(Q′_i) and [ℓN]P′_i = [ℓ]Q′_i, (ii) Z′_{π′(P′_i)} contains no positive-dimensional coset, (iii) if Q′_i ∈ Y′ and P′_i is not isolated in X′ ∩ [ℓN]^{-1}([ℓ]Y′) then Q′_i ∈ Y′ ∩ (Y′ − im σ) for some non-zero ℓ-torsion section σ.
items.locator: Lemma 8.2, (8.1)–(8.8) and proof, pp.42–45, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprints E14)
items.note: Local parametrizations of X and Z at P composed with a lift of the Betti map give φ₁, φ₂; Proposition 6.1(v) gives δ₀(0) ≠ 0 and Proposition 7.2 with N₀ = ℓ gives the pairs. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Auxiliary sets Σ_k of intersections with torsion translates
items.statement: Σ₀ = components of Z′; Σ_{k+1} = components of Y′ ∩ (Y′ − im σ) for Y′ ∈ Σ_k and σ ∈ 𝒜′[ℓ](S′) with Y′ ⊄ Y′ − im σ. Then dim Y′ ≤ n − k and deg Y′_t ≤ D^{2^k} for Y′ ∈ Σ_k, so deg Y′_t ≤ D^{2^{g+1}} on Σ = Σ₀ ∪ ⋯ ∪ Σ_n, independently of ℓ (8.9).
items.locator: §8.3, (i)–(iii) and (8.9), pp.45–46, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Fibre degrees over special points by conservation of number. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Proposition 8.1 (many isolated division points)
items.statement: If X ⊆ 𝒜 is irreducible closed over F, dominates S and is not generically special, there are c > 0, a finite étale S′ → S and closed Y₁,…,Y_R ⊆ 𝒜′ = 𝒜 ×_S S′ such that for every integer N ≥ c^{-1} some Y_j has X′ ∩ [N]^{-1}(Y_j) with at least cN^{2 dim X} irreducible components of dimension 0.
items.locator: Proposition 8.1, p.42; proof pp.46–47, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Take Y = [ℓ]^{-1}([ℓ]Y′) for the Y′ ∈ Σ hit most often; a non-isolated point would force a σ(t)-stable fibre and a positive-dimensional stabilizer, contradicting Lemma 8.2(ii). Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Lemma 9.2 (auxiliary rational map)
items.statement: For locally closed X, Y ⊆ ℙ^M with X irreducible there is δ depending only on Y such that for any Q₁,…,Q_r ∈ X ∩ Y there are forms ϕ₀,…,ϕ_{dim X} of degree δ with common zero set 𝒵 such that ϕ = [ϕ₀:⋯:ϕ_{dim X}] maps Y∖𝒵 to [1:0:⋯:0], the Q_i ∉ 𝒵, and any irreducible C ⊆ X through some Q_i on which ϕ is constant lies in the closure of Y.
items.locator: Lemma 9.2 and proof, pp.47–48, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Lemma 9.3 (isolated points bound the degree; Habegger)
items.statement: For a rational map ϕ : X ⇢ ℙ^{dim X}_ℂ on an irreducible variety, the number of zero-dimensional components of any fibre ϕ^{-1}(Q) is at most deg ϕ (deg ϕ = 0 if ϕ is not dominant).
items.locator: Lemma 9.3, p.48, citing Habegger [Hab13, Lemma 4.2], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Lemma 9.4 (height lower bound from degree; Habegger)
items.statement: For X ⊆ ℙ^M irreducible closed over Q̄ of positive dimension and ϕ = [ϕ₀:⋯:ϕ_{dim X}] given by forms of equal degree ≤ D not all vanishing on X, there are c and a Zariski open dense U ⊆ X on which the ϕ_i have no common zero and h(ϕ(P)) ≥ (4^{dim X} deg X)^{-1} (deg ϕ / D^{dim X − 1}) h(P) − c.
items.locator: Lemma 9.4, p.49, citing Habegger [Hab13, Lemma 4.3], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Silverman: heights under generically finite dominant maps
items.statement: For a dominant generically finite morphism (or equidimensional dominant rational map) f : X′ → X of varieties over Q̄ there are c > 0, c′ and a Zariski open dense U with h(f(P)) ≥ c h(P) − c′ on U (Silverman, J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 26 (2011)).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 9.1, p.49, citing [Sil11], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Used to pass through the finite étale cover S′ → S. Routed to RP.0 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 9.1 (height inequality in the total space)
items.statement: If X ⊆ 𝒜 is irreducible closed, dominates S and is not generically special, there is c > 0 such that for every integer N ≥ c^{-1} there are a non-empty Zariski open U_N ⊆ X and c′(N) with h([2^N]Q) ≥ c4^N h(Q) − c′(N) for all Q ∈ U_N(Q̄).
items.locator: Proposition 9.1, p.47; proof pp.49–51, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Proposition 8.1 with 2^N gives ≥ c₃4^{N dim X} isolated points in a fibre of ϕ ∘ [2^N] (Lemma 9.2); Lemma 9.3 bounds deg(ϕ ∘ [2^N]) below, Lemma 9.4 with degree ≤ c₂δ4^N and (9.2) conclude. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Silverman–Tate theorem (line-bundle version)
items.statement: For an abelian scheme with admissible immersion there is c₁ ≥ 0 with |ĥ_𝒜(P) − h(P)| ≤ c₁(1 + h(π(P))) for all P ∈ 𝒜(Q̄); the smoothness hypothesis of [Sil83, Thm. A] can be dropped when working with line bundles instead of Weil divisors.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 10.1, (10.2), p.51, citing Silverman [Sil83, Thm. A], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source, as for PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 (which reproves it).

items.name: Proposition 10.1 (Néron–Tate height versus naive height)
items.statement: If X ⊆ 𝒜 is irreducible closed and not generically special, there are a non-empty Zariski open U ⊆ X over Q̄ and c > 0 with h(P) ≤ c(1 + ĥ_𝒜(P)) for all P ∈ U(Q̄).
items.locator: Proposition 10.1 and proof, pp.51–52, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Silverman–Tate plus Proposition 9.1: ĥ_𝒜(P) ≥ (c₂ − c₁/4^N)h(P) − (c₃(N) + c₁)/4^N, then fix N with 4^N ≥ 2c₁/c₂ ("killing Zimmer constants"). Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Theorem 11.1 (Silverman's Height Limit Theorem, after base change)
items.statement: For x ∈ A(K̄) represented by σ_x : S′ → 𝒜 over a generically finite ρ : S′ → S, lim ĥ_𝒜(σ_x(t)) / h_S(ρ(t)) = ĥ_{K,A}(x) as h_S(ρ(t)) → ∞, with h_S = h ∘ ι / deg S (11.1). Heights on curves are quasi-equivalent (h_S ∘ ρ / h_{S′} → deg ρ) and ĥ_{K′,A_{K′}} = [K′:K] ĥ_{K,A}.
items.locator: Theorem 11.1, (11.1)–(11.2) and proof, pp.52–53, citing Silverman [Sil83, Thm. B], Bombieri–Gubler Cor. 9.3.10 and [Con06, Rem. 9.2], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprints E16)
items.note: Routed to RP.0 as a source.

items.name: Moriwaki heights over finitely generated fields and their height machine
items.statement: For k₀ finitely generated over ℚ of transcendence degree d with a polarization B = (B; H̄₁,…,H̄_d; τ) (B flat quasi-projective integral over ℤ, H̄_i nef smooth hermitian line bundles), and a line bundle L on a projective X over k₀, the Moriwaki height h^B_{k₀,X,L} : X(k₀‾) → ℝ, defined up to O(1), satisfies additivity, functoriality under quasi-finite morphisms, boundedness below off the base locus, Northcott when L is ample and B is big, and the algebraic-equivalence limit (Proposition A.1); it transforms correctly under isomorphisms of k₀.
items.locator: §A.1, (A.1) and Proposition A.1, pp.54–55, citing Moriwaki [Mor00, Prop. 3.3.7], Wazir [Waz06, Prop. 2(iv)], Lang [Lan83, Ch. 4, Prop. 3.3, Cor. 3.4], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII, whose Yuan–Zhang adelic line bundles over finitely generated fields contain Moriwaki's heights.

items.name: Proposition A.2 (Moriwaki Néron–Tate height)
items.statement: For A over k₀ with symmetric ample L, ĥ^B_L(P) = lim 2^{-2n} h^B_L([2^n]P) exists, is quadratic, ≥ 0, vanishes on torsion, and when B is big vanishes exactly on torsion points.
items.locator: (A.2) and Proposition A.2, pp.55–56, citing [Mor00, §3.4, Prop. 3.4.1], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII.

items.name: Silverman–Tate and the height limit theorem for Moriwaki heights (Wazir)
items.statement: The Silverman–Tate comparison and Silverman's specialization limit (11.2) hold with Moriwaki heights in place of Weil heights ([Waz06, Thms. 2, 3]).
items.locator: §A.2, p.56; §A.3, p.57, citing Wazir [Waz06], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII.

items.name: Theorem A.3 (height inequality with Moriwaki heights)
items.statement: For k₀ finitely generated over ℚ with polarization B, an abelian scheme 𝒜 → S over a smooth irreducible quasi-projective curve over k₀‾, L symmetric relatively ample, M ample on S̄ and X ⊆ 𝒜 closed irreducible, there is c > 0 depending on B, 𝒜/S, X, L, M with h^B_{S̄,M}(π(P)) ≤ c(1 + ĥ^B_{𝒜,L}(P)) for P ∈ X*(k₀‾).
items.locator: Theorem A.3 and sketch, p.56, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Repeat §§9–10 with Proposition A.1 and Wazir's Silverman–Tate; reduce to k₀ ⊆ ℂ by an isomorphism. Routed to the uniformity Part II.

items.name: Essential minimum under extension of the constant field
items.statement: For X ⊆ A over k₀‾(S): µ_ess(X) = 0 iff ĥ(X) = 0 (Zhang's inequalities in Gubler's function-field form [Gub07, Cor. 4.4]); the canonical height of a subvariety is unchanged by extending the constant field k₀‾ to k, so µ_ess(X_K) = 0 implies µ_ess(X) = 0.
items.locator: §A.3, p.57, citing Zhang [Zha95] and Gubler [Gub07, Cor. 4.4, §3], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (a sketch)
items.note: Routed to the uniformity Part II with Theorem 1.1 for general k.

items.name: Bogomolov: maximal cosets in a subvariety have bounded degree
items.statement: For a subvariety X of an abelian variety A ⊆ ℙ^M over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, the maximal cosets contained in X are translates of abelian subvarieties of degree bounded in terms of deg X, A and the polarization ([Bog81, Thm. 1]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition C.1, p.61, citing Bogomolov [Bog81], arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Routed to RP.5 as a source, as for PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26.

items.name: Lemma C.2 and (C.1) (hypersurfaces containing no translate of B)
items.statement: H_V(d) ≥ binom(dim V + d, dim V) ≥ d + 1 for the Hilbert function of V ⊆ ℙ^M with dim V ≥ 1 (C.1). For A ⊆ ℙ^M of dimension g ≥ 2, an abelian subvariety B with dim B ≥ 1 and d ≥ max{1, g − dim B}, the degree-d forms f such that A ∩ 𝒵(f) contains a translate of B lie in a closed subset of codimension ≥ d + 1 + dim B − g.
items.locator: (C.1) and Lemma C.2 with proof, pp.59–61, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019)
items.note: Incidence variety and fibre dimension counts. Routed to RP.5 as a source.

items.name: Proposition C.1 (hyperbolic hypersurface sections of abelian varieties)
items.statement: For A ⊆ ℙ^M of dimension g ≥ 1 and d ≥ g − 1, there is a Zariski open dense U in the space of degree-d forms, with complement of codimension ≥ d + 2 − g, such that A ∩ 𝒵(f) contains no positive-dimensional coset for f ∈ U. Hence for d ≥ g a generic degree-d section through a given point is hyperbolic (by Bloch–Ochiai).
items.locator: Proposition C.1, its corollary and proof, pp.59, 61, arXiv v3 (28 January 2019) (misprint E17)
items.note: A quantitative case of Brotbek's theorem: Bogomolov reduces to finitely many B, and Lemma C.2 handles each. Routed to RP.5 as a source.
